name: Vega 2
best_known_for: Sibling of Vega 1 — second Soviet Venus + Halley combination probe, dropped a lander + balloon at Venus then flew past Halley 3 days after Vega 1
credit: Identical twin of Vega 1, launched 1984-12-21 (6 days after Vega 1) from Baikonur on a Proton-K / D-1. 4920 kg flyby bus + ~1500 kg descent module with second Venera-style lander + helium aerostat. Venus arrival 1985-06-15: lander touched down at 8.5°S, 164.5°E (Aphrodite Terra), returned 57 minutes of surface science before failure; balloon floated in the cloud deck for 46 hours alongside Vega 1's. The flyby bus continued on its 9-month cruise and encountered comet 1P/Halley 1986-03-09 at 8030 km — the second Halley encounter of the armada, 3 days after Vega 1 and 5 days before Giotto. Vega 1 + Vega 2 data was the basis for Giotto's much closer Halley approach: ESA used the Soviet tracking to refine the nucleus position to within 50 km.

links.l: Sagdeev et al. (1986) — Vega + the Halley armada (Nature 321)
